text: Dr. Sher Afgan Khan Niazi (Urdu: شیر افگن خان نیازی; died 11 October 2012) was a Pakistani politician who served as Minister of Parliamentary Affairs of Pakistan. His real uncle was AK Niazi, also known as General Niazi. He was elected for a fourth time to the National Assembly in 2002 as a member of the Pakistan Peoples Party (Parliamentarians), but later switched his allegiance to the PPPP (Patriot) and then joined the Pakistan Muslim League (Q). Sher Afgan Niazi supported President Pervez Musharraf's actions in 2007, including the ousting, detention, and replacement of Supreme Court judges, and backed Musharraf's military operation at Lal Masjid in Islamabad. On 18 February 2008, he lost the general election to independent candidate Humair Hayat Khan Rokhri. On April 8, 2008, he was attacked in Lahore, Punjab, by lawyers protesting against his support for the dismissal of Supreme Court judges and the Lal Masjid operation, an incident that sparked strong protests in his home town. Niazi joined President Pervez Musharraf's newly formed political party, the All Pakistan Muslim League (APML), but later resigned due to differences with the party leadership. He was highly knowledgeable in constitutional affairs and had a strong command over the Constitution of Pakistan. He completed his M.B.B.S degree from Nishtar Medical College in Multan, Punjab. Niazi was known for memorizing all the articles of the Constitution of Pakistan. His health declined gradually after one of his sons died in a car accident in Rawalpindi, and he was diagnosed with liver cancer in 2012.
